section: IVC town planning - grid layout, citadel and lower town, drainage, Great Bath, granaries
subsections: Drainage - covered drains, manholes, soak pits
Dholavira - three-part plan, water harvesting, rock-cut features

accepted.s: Which feature is regarded as the most advanced feature of the Indus Valley Civilization towns?
accepted.x: The planned drainage system is regarded as the most advanced feature of Indus Valley Civilization towns.
accepted.tq: Use direct recall for a high-yield superlative fact.
accepted.sec: Drainage - covered drains, manholes, soak pits

accepted.s: The correct sequence of wastewater movement in an Indus Valley settlement was:
o: Soak pits → house drains → street drains → main channels
House drains → street drains → soak pits or main channels
Main channels → street drains → house drains → soak pits
Street drains → house drains → soak pits → main channels
accepted.x: Wastewater generally moved from house drains into street drains and then into soak pits or main channels.
accepted.tq: Trace the functional sequence from source to outlet.
accepted.sec: Drainage - covered drains, manholes, soak pits

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Indus Valley drainage systems:
1. Drains were generally covered.
2. Manholes were provided for cleaning.
3. Burnt bricks and terracotta pipes were used in their construction.
4. Streets were designed with a slope to facilitate natural flow.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Covered drains had manholes for maintenance, were built with burnt bricks and terracotta pipes, and used street slopes for natural flow.
accepted.tq: Check whether all statements describe connected features of one civic system.
accepted.sec: Drainage - covered drains, manholes, soak pits

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about drainage in smaller Indus Valley settlements is correct?
o: Planned drainage was confined to the largest cities.
Kalibangan had wooden drains, whereas Banawali lacked a systematic drainage system.
Banawali had the most elaborate drainage system and Kalibangan had none.
Both Kalibangan and Banawali used only stone drains.
accepted.x: Planned drainage existed even in small settlements. Kalibangan had wooden drains, while Banawali lacked a systematic drainage system.
accepted.tq: Separate the two similar settlement examples by assigning each its distinctive feature.
accepted.sec: Drainage - covered drains, manholes, soak pits

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Water reservoirs, dams and embankments — Harappa
accepted.x: Water reservoirs, dams and embankments are associated with Dholavira, not Harappa.
accepted.tq: Find the location mismatch by comparing each structure with its known site.

accepted.s: The dockyard of the Indus Valley Civilization is associated with:
accepted.x: The dockyard, whose function has also been debated as possibly an irrigation tank, is associated with Lothal.

accepted.s: Fire altars in the Indus Valley Civilization are associated with:
accepted.x: Fire altars have been identified at Kalibangan, including seven such altars, and at Lothal.
accepted.tq: Test a paired site association directly.

accepted.s: Dholavira is distinguished among the known Indus Valley cities because it was divided into:
o: Four parts—citadel, market, temple and lower town
Three parts—citadel, middle town and lower town
accepted.x: Dholavira is described as the only Indus Valley city divided into three parts: citadel, middle town and lower town.
accepted.tq: Use the unique qualifier to distinguish Dholavira from other planned cities.
accepted.sec: Dholavira - three-part plan, water harvesting, rock-cut features  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about water management at Dholavira:
1. It included giant reservoirs.
2. Bunds or check-dams and channels fed the reservoirs.
3. Dams and embankments formed part of the system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Dholavira had giant reservoirs supplied through bunds, check-dams and channels, along with dams and embankments.
accepted.tq: Recognise a complete cluster of related water-management features.
accepted.sec: Dholavira - three-part plan, water harvesting, rock-cut features  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the construction materials and techniques associated with Dholavira?
o: Its reservoirs were partly cut into rock, and sandstone and limestone blocks were used for major construction.
It used only baked bricks, unlike Mohenjodaro and Harappa.
Its major structures were built exclusively of iron and copper.
Its reservoirs were entirely made of timber and mud.
accepted.x: Some Dholavira reservoirs were partly cut into the rock, and sandstone and limestone blocks were used for major construction. Mohenjodaro and Harappa are contrasted with it for their use of baked brick.
accepted.tq: Use the material contrast to distinguish Dholavira from Mohenjodaro and Harappa.
accepted.sec: Dholavira - three-part plan, water harvesting, rock-cut features  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following features is associated with Dholavira in addition to its reservoirs and water-management works?
o: A multi-pillared assembly hall and wooden drains
A stadium or ceremonial ground and a signboard inscription
A tidal dockyard and seven fire altars
accepted.x: Dholavira had a stadium or ceremonial ground and a signboard inscription in addition to its reservoirs and related hydraulic works.
accepted.tq: Combine distinctive features of one site while rejecting features belonging to other sites.
accepted.sec: Dholavira - three-part plan, water harvesting, rock-cut features  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The largest Indus Valley inscription, consisting of a ten-sign signboard, has been reported from the:
accepted.x: The largest inscription is the ten-sign signboard found at the North Gate of Dholavira.
accepted.tq: Link the numerical detail with its exact site and location.

accepted.s: The ceremonial ground or stadium at Dholavira measured approximately:
accepted.x: The stadium or ceremonial ground at Dholavira measured approximately 283 × 47 metres.
accepted.tq: Retain both dimensions rather than identifying the structure by name alone.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the five largest Harappan cities listed in connection with Dholavira?
accepted.x: The five listed cities are Dholavira, Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Ganweriwala and Rakhigarhi. Kalibangan is not included in that list.
accepted.tq: Use exclusion from a named list and watch for a nearby Harappan site.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Dholavira:
1. It had 16 reservoirs.
2. The reservoirs covered about 10 per cent of the site.
3. The largest reservoir measured approximately 73 × 29 metres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Dholavira had 16 reservoirs covering about 10 per cent of the site, and the largest measured approximately 73 × 29 metres.
accepted.tq: Combine count, proportion and dimensions in a quantitative statement set.

accepted.s: Dholavira was occupied through seven stages during approximately which period?
accepted.x: Dholavira was occupied through seven stages from approximately 3000 to 1500 BCE.
accepted.tq: Match the duration and date range rather than relying on a single year.

accepted.s: Which of the following best explains the significance of standardised bricks, grid planning and drainage in the Indus Valley Civilization?
o: They suggest civic authority and early engineering skill.
They prove that all settlements were royal capitals.
They show that the civilization had abandoned urban planning.
They indicate the exclusive control of religious institutions.
accepted.x: Standardisation of bricks, grid planning and drainage points to civic authority and considerable early engineering skill.
accepted.tq: Infer the institutional significance from the combination of urban features.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Indus Valley and contemporary West Asian civilizations:
1. No palaces or temples have been clearly identified in the Indus Valley cities.
2. Indus Valley drainage was more advanced than that of contemporary Mesopotamia and Egypt.
3. The absence of clearly identified palaces or temples proves that the Indus Valley Civilization had no civic authority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The absence of clearly identified palaces or temples does not disprove civic authority; standardised urban planning instead suggests it.
accepted.tq: Reject an overextended conclusion while retaining the supported comparative statements.

accepted.s: Which one of the following comparisons is correct?
o: All three sites used exactly the same construction material for major structures.
Dholavira used only baked brick, whereas Mohenjodaro and Harappa used sandstone and limestone.
Mohenjodaro and Harappa had rock-cut reservoirs, whereas Dholavira had none.
Dholavira used sandstone and limestone blocks for major construction, whereas Mohenjodaro and Harappa are associated with baked-brick construction.
accepted.x: Dholavira used sandstone and limestone blocks for major construction and had partly rock-cut reservoirs, while Mohenjodaro and Harappa are contrasted with it for baked-brick construction.
accepted.tq: Identify the correctly reversed comparison between related urban centres.
accepted.sec: Dholavira - three-part plan, water harvesting, rock-cut features  [other exams, GROUP-II]
